title: Where the ACF decays, the PACF cuts off: partial autocorrelation (a newly-authored op) vs statsmodels

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The partial autocorrelation function (PACF) is the companion of the ACF: where the ACF decays, the PACF cuts off after the autoregressive order, making it the standard tool for AR model selection. Having just added the ACF, this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED PACF op (Durbin-Levinson on the biased ACF). On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel it reproduces the field-standard statsmodels.tsa.pacf(method='ldb') BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~6e-15) across lags; the lag-1 PACF exactly equals the lag-1 ACF (0.856, the definitional identity), and the lag-2 PACF is strongly negative (-0.627) -- the signature of an oscillatory AR(2)-like process, exactly what eyes-closed posterior alpha (a resonant ~10 Hz rhythm) looks like.

claims.statement: partial autocorrelation at lag 1 -- equals the lag-1 autocorrelation
partial autocorrelation at lag 2 -- strongly negative (oscillatory AR(2)-like alpha structure)
partial autocorrelation at lag 0 -- 1 by convention

validation.reference: The newly-authored partialAutocorrelation op is validated against the field-standard statsmodels.tsa.pacf(method='ldb') on the identical signal. Both run the Durbin-Levinson recursion on the biased demeaned ACF; the agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~6e-15) across lags. The lag-1 PACF equals the lag-1 ACF (the identity) and the lag-2 PACF is strongly negative (an oscillatory AR(2)-like structure).
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), subject S002 run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored partialAutocorrelation reproduces statsmodels.tsa.pacf(method='ldb') bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~6e-15) across lags; (2) the lag-1 PACF equals the lag-1 ACF (the identity) and the lag-2 PACF is strongly negative. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED, building on the just-added autocorrelation, to complete the ACF/PACF pair -- the ecosystem had neither the single-series ACF nor the PACF; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and statsmodels run the IDENTICAL Levinson-Durbin recursion on the biased ACF, so the ~6e-15 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement (this matches the 'ldb'/'ywm' biased conventions; statsmodels' unbiased 'yw'/'ld' and 'ols' differ by construction and are NOT the target); (3) the finding is the AR structure: the lag-1 PACF exactly equals the lag-1 ACF (the definitional identity), and the lag-2 PACF is strongly NEGATIVE, the signature of an oscillatory AR(2)-like process -- exactly what eyes-closed posterior alpha looks like (a resonant ~10 Hz rhythm); (4) the value is a signal property (dimensionless); the reproducible content is the bit-exact PACF and the AR structure, not an absolute physiological constant; (5) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The PACF's cut-off lag is the classic AR order estimate; feeding it (and the ACF) into an explicit AR-model fit (Yule-Walker / Burg) with an information-criterion order selection would turn this pair into a parametric-spectrum layer (an AR spectral estimate complementing the Welch PSD already folded). Documented, not escalated.
